fullPassage: Have you ever felt bored, even though you were busy and successful? In his book The Big Leap, Gay Hendricks presents a framework that divides the activities in our lives into four zones. The first is the Zone of Incompetence: things we are simply not good at. They can frustrate and exhaust us. The second is the Zone of Competence: things we can do well enough, but many other people could do just as well. These activities may not be especially exciting or satisfying. The third is the Zone of Excellence, where many successful people spend much of their time. These are skills we have mastered, and we are often rewarded and praised for them. Yet Hendricks calls this zone "a trap." We may look successful on the outside, but we can feel empty or exhausted on the inside. Because this zone feels safe and rewarding, it can be difficult to leave. The fourth is the Zone of Genius: the unique place where our special abilities, what we love to do, and the value we create come together. In this zone, we may feel deeply engaged in what we are doing. Time can seem to fly, and even hard work may feel almost effortless. Hendricks also describes the Upper Limit Problem. He suggests that people sometimes create problems for themselves when they begin to experience more happiness or success than they are comfortable with. They may worry, procrastinate, or even start conflicts without fully realizing why. He sees this resistance as a sign that we may be approaching a personal limit on how much success or happiness we are comfortable with. So how can we spend more time in our Zone of Genius? Hendricks suggests starting with just ten minutes a day and gradually giving more time to activities in this zone. In The Big Leap, he describes spending 70 percent or more of his time in his Zone of Genius as a possible long-term goal. The idea is to begin with a small step and gradually make more room for activities that use our strengths and give us energy.

questions.passage: Have you ever felt bored, even though you were busy and successful? In his book The Big Leap, Gay Hendricks presents a framework that divides the activities in our lives into four zones. The first is the Zone of Incompetence: things we are simply not good at. They can frustrate and exhaust us. The second is the Zone of Competence: things we can do well enough, but many other people could do just as well. These activities may not be especially exciting or satisfying. The third is the Zone of Excellence, where many successful people spend much of their time. These are skills we have mastered, and we are often rewarded and praised for them. Yet Hendricks calls this zone "a trap." We may look successful on the outside, but we can feel empty or exhausted on the inside. Because this zone feels safe and rewarding, it can be difficult to leave. The fourth is the Zone of Genius: the unique place where our special abilities, what we love to do, and the value we create come together. In this zone, we may feel deeply engaged in what we are doing. Time can seem to fly, and even hard work may feel almost effortless. Hendricks also describes the Upper Limit Problem. He suggests that people sometimes create problems for themselves when they begin to experience more happiness or success than they are comfortable with. They may worry, procrastinate, or even start conflicts without fully realizing why. He sees this resistance as a sign that we may be approaching a personal limit on how much success or happiness we are comfortable with. So how can we spend more time in our Zone of Genius? Hendricks suggests starting with just ten minutes a day and gradually giving more time to activities in this zone. In The Big Leap, he describes spending 70 percent or more of his time in his Zone of Genius as a possible long-term goal. The idea is to begin with a small step and gradually make more room for activities that use our strengths and give us energy.

❌ ② Success always brings happiness without any inner resistance.(성공은 내적 저항 없이 언제나 행복을 가져다준다): 상한선 문제 — 성공이 커질 때 오히려 저항이 생긴다 — 와 정반대

❌ ③ People should quit their jobs immediately.(당장 일을 그만두어야 한다): 하루 10분의 '작은 걸음'으로 시작하라는 조언과 정반대

✅ ④ We should gradually make more room for activities that use our unique strengths.(우리의 고유한 강점을 쓰는 활동에 점차 더 많은 자리를 내어 주어야 한다): 마지막 문장의 결론과 정확히 일치 ← 정답
